topics.title: Introduction to React & Prerequisites
topics.content:
React is a declarative, efficient, and flexible open-source JavaScript library developed by Facebook for building user interfaces, specifically Single Page Applications (SPAs). It allows developers to create reusable UI components.

Prerequisites: Before learning React, you should have a solid understanding of HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript (ES6+), including concepts like arrow functions, classes, array destructuring, modules (import/export), and template literals.
topics.interviewTip: When asked: 'What is React?', don't just say it is a framework. Emphasize that React is a **library** focused solely on the View layer of an application, utilizing a Virtual DOM to optimize rendering performance.

topics.title: Installation & Project Structure
topics.content:
A modern React project is typically initialized using build tools like Vite (or previously Create React App):

npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev

File Structure:

  • package.json: Defines project dependencies and scripts.
  • index.html: The main HTML entry point with a root div (<div id="root"></div>).
  • src/main.jsx: Mounts the React application to the root div.
  • src/App.jsx: The main application component.

topics.title: JSX (JavaScript XML)
topics.content:
JSX is a syntax extension to JavaScript that looks similar to HTML. React uses JSX to describe what the UI should look like. JSX compiles down to standard JavaScript React.createElement() calls.

Rules of JSX:

  • All tags must be closed (e.g., <img />, <br />).
  • A component must return a single root element. We can wrap multiple elements in a React Fragment (<>...</>).
  • Use className instead of class, and htmlFor instead of for.

topics.title: JavaScript Variables & Comments in JSX
topics.content:
You can embed any JavaScript expression in JSX by wrapping it in curly braces { }:

const name = 'Aritra';
const element = <h1>Hello, {name}!</h1>;

Comments in JSX: Inside JSX tags, comments must be wrapped in curly braces and use block comments style:

{/* This is a comment in JSX */}

topics.title: React Components: Functional vs Class
topics.content:
Components are the building blocks of React. There are two primary types:

  • Functional Components: Simple JavaScript functions that accept props and return JSX. They utilize Hooks (like useState) to manage state.
    • function Welcome(props) {
  return <h1>Hello, {props.name}</h1>;
}
  • Class Components: ES6 classes that extend React.Component and require a render() method. They manage state via this.state. (Legacy, but still found in older systems).
    • class Welcome extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <h1>Hello, {this.props.name}</h1>;
  }
}

practiceQuestions.question: What is React and what are its key features?
practiceQuestions.answer: React is an open-source JavaScript library developed by Facebook for building user interfaces. Its key features include: (1) Component-Based Architecture (reusable widgets), (2) Virtual DOM (optimized rendering), (3) Declarative UI, and (4) Unidirectional Data Flow.

practiceQuestions.question: What is JSX? Explain three strict syntax rules of JSX.
practiceQuestions.answer: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It is a syntax extension for JavaScript that allows writing HTML-like code inside JS. Rules: (1) Every tag must be self-closing or closed explicitly. (2) It must return a single parent element (or a Fragment `<>...</>`). (3) HTML attributes must use camelCase conventions, such as `className` instead of `class` and `tabIndex` instead of `tabindex`.

practiceQuestions.question: How do you embed variables and write comments inside a JSX block? Provide code snippets.
Differentiate between Functional Components and Class Components in React.
practiceQuestions.answer: Functional components are plain JavaScript functions that accept props and return JSX; they use Hooks to manage state and lifecycles. Class components are ES6 classes extending `React.Component`, require a `render()` method, and manage state/lifecycles via class methods (`this.state`, `componentDidMount`). Functional components are the modern standard.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the purpose of React Fragments?
practiceQuestions.answer: React components must return a single root element. When we want to group multiple sibling components without adding an extra wrapper node (like an unnecessary `<div>` that clutter the DOM and affects CSS flex/grid layouts), we wrap them in a React Fragment: `<React.Fragment>...</React.Fragment>` or the shorthand `<>...</>`.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a key architectural feature of React?
mcqs.explanation: React uses a Virtual DOM which is a lightweight copy of the real DOM. When state changes, React updates the Virtual DOM first, runs a diffing algorithm, and updates the real DOM only where necessary.

mcqs.question: JSX gets compiled down to which standard JavaScript calls?
mcqs.explanation: Babel/Vite compiles JSX code into standard nested `React.createElement(type, props, ...children)` function calls.

mcqs.question: Which attribute must be used in JSX to define a CSS class?
mcqs.explanation: Wait, 'class' is a reserved keyword in JavaScript. In JSX, we must use 'className' instead of 'class' to avoid compiler issues.

mcqs.question: Wait! What is the correct answer to the above question?
mcqs.explanation: className must be used in JSX since class is a reserved keyword in JS.

mcqs.question: How do you write comments inside a JSX rendering block?
mcqs.explanation: Inside JSX templates, comments must be wrapped in curly braces and use JS multi-line comments: `{/* ... */}`.

mcqs.question: Which React hook is used to introduce local state variables in a functional component?
mcqs.explanation: useState is the core React Hook that lets functional components hold and modify component-local state.

mcqs.question: In React, what are 'props'?
options: Read-only properties passed from a parent component down to child components
States that can be modified by the component itself
mcqs.explanation: Props (short for properties) are inputs passed down from parent components to child components and are immutable inside the receiver.

mcqs.question: Class components require which method to return the component's JSX layout?
mcqs.explanation: All React Class components must implement a `render()` method that returns the JSX nodes describing the component UI.

mcqs.question: What is the shorthand syntax for React Fragments?
mcqs.explanation: Empty angle brackets `<>...</>` serve as the shorthand syntactic sugar for `<React.Fragment>...</React.Fragment>`.

mcqs.question: In a React project, what is the role of index.html?
options: It compiles the entire JavaScript code
It serves as the single page frame containing the target div where React mounts the component tree
mcqs.explanation:
React is an SPA library. index.html acts as the static shell containing a target container (usually `
`) where the JS engine mounts the virtual DOM.

mcqs.question: Which prerequisite JS concept is critical for importing other files and components in React?
mcqs.explanation: React applications are structured as modular files. We use ES6 `import Header from './Header'` and `export default App` to share components across files.
